decision: What has run is observed by this observatory alone: the lab asks it to observe what has run every quarter hour, and its voice says what newly comes into view here - urgently where the lens of signs says so. A part observed writes only its own tables. ocoeco is taken from its release, checked against its sums, in seconds where building it took minutes.
why: Sign runs-are-observed-twice (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco): the lab observed what had run on its own every quarter hour, beside this observatory, because this observatory observed only every six hours and on landings - too seldom to hear in time that something broke. Looked at first: the observation that is the place's own is this one - its record keeps what it saw, and its page is made from it; the lab's was there for timing only. Tried before: observing a part rewrote what the whole had found (decision 2026-11-14-a-part-observed-speaks-for-itself in ocoeco).
rejected: The lab observing and pushing what it saw here (one more writer of this record); this observatory observing every quarter hour on its own schedule (GitHub's schedule is seldom kept that often); keeping both and quieting one voice by a rule.

decision: Every line of what followed leads somewhere: the site lays out a page for each thing the author said that work followed - offered by the conversation's place, and placed here - and a page for each record of work of the last three days and each thing such a record entered or changed, beside the pages for places, signs, angles of the form and decisions a sign came to. A page of a thing says the thing in full, and what is around it.
why: Opened on what followed, the front showed lines one could read and not step on: a decision, a reflection, a record of work had no page, and the line about it was only text - a dead surface in small. What a look shows is where one goes on from.
rejected: A page for every thing in view (ten thousand of them, laid out anew at each observing, to say what nobody steps to); pages only for what the latest turn touched (the turn before it would lead nowhere the moment the author speaks again).

decision: The page this observatory shows first opens on what followed the latest thing the author said - the lens the conversation's place brings, placed before the sheet: his words, and what was done, seen, learned, entered and released since. Then the sheet, the perfect form, and every other lens.
why: What the author looks for first when he comes back is what came of what he last said - and until now he read it as text the agent wrote in a chat. On his own page it is read off the records of work, each line about a thing one can step to, and it is there whether or not anyone wrote it.
rejected: A page of its own, linked from the front (what he looks for first would be a step away, and the front would open on what he did not ask); placing it after the sheet (the sheet says what waits - mostly on him - and changes little from one thing he says to the next; what followed is new each time).

decision: ocoeco is taken from its newest release that has its files. A release is made first and its files are built after it: for those minutes the newest release has nothing to take, and the one before it serves.
why: On 2026-11-15 a run failed on main: asked to observe a minute after ocoeco 0.49.0 was released, it found no files to download. Five releases were made that day, each opening such a gap of a few minutes, and the lab asks this observatory to observe every quarter hour.
rejected: Building ocoeco from its source here (minutes, where taking it is seconds); waiting in this workflow until the files are there (a wait of unknown length, for something the release before already gives); leaving it (a run failing on main is a sign on the sheet, and this one would be about nothing in this place).

decision: The pages are laid out and published where the whole was observed - four times a day, and whenever an observing is asked for. An observing of one part only - what has run, asked for by the lab every quarter hour - keeps what it observed and leaves the pages as they are.
why: With a page for each thing the author said, each record of work of late and each thing it touched, the site is over a thousand pages and takes six minutes to lay out. Laid out anew at every quarter hour, the observatory was laying out pages most of the time, each observing waiting on the one before: on 2026-11-15 a job that waited for none to be under way waited a quarter of an hour. What the quarter hour is for is that the lab's sheet sees what has run - and that is in what is kept, not on the page.
rejected: Fewer pages (that every line leads somewhere is what the pages are for); leaving it (an observing asked for after a change waits behind the quarter hours, and the same pages are laid out ninety-six times a day to say what changed four times).
